summary: Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS University of London, later serving there as a research fellow (1999–2002), teaching at Oxford, and joining the University of British Columbia (~2005).

Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He served as President of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Adeu Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, holding a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsu-lin Mei was a scholar in linguistics and sinology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1952–1954), Harvard University (~1955–1958), and Yale University (~1958–1962), and later held posts at Harvard (~1964–1970) and Cornell University (~1970–2000).

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington under Christopher I. Beckwith and others, later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1997–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held lecturer posts at Rissho and served as President of Reiyukai (~1971–1996, ~2000–2017) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1985–2018).
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima works in indology and history and archaeology. After earning his undergraduate and graduate degrees at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Allione specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Antioch University and under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, Apho Rinpoche, Abo Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), with additional research affiliations at Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1971) and held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1976–1995) and Kyoto University (~1995–2007).
Tsuruji Sahoda was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) and held positions at Ritsumeikan University (~1928–1949) and Osaka University (~1949–1963).
Tsutomu Hatai worked in Indology. He served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society (attested 1987), succeeding Hiroshi Maruyama.
Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1990).

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar. He studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912) and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University, holding posts at Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Hokkaido University. He has held researcher posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and held a post as a project researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).
